Script fixed 2026-10-14 per fact-check.md; Policyholders' Interests master circular 2024, Implementation of Ombudsman Award (iv). Add 'Unless the company challenges the award' (fact-check.md).

claim: If you are not happy with the award, you can still go to a consumer court
source_quote: The award of Insurance Ombudsman shall be binding on the insurers (or insurance broker, as the case may be). However, if the complainant is not satisfied with the decision of the Insurance Ombudsman, he/she may exercise the right to take recourse to the normal process of law against the Insurance Company/Insurance Broker.
note: v2 re-check 2026-10-14: cut in v2: v1 H065 (consumer court after the award) was dropped; E052 only says you do not need a consumer court case (HC-19). Put the consumer-court option in the description. CIO FAQ Q21. A consumer commission is one route under 'the normal process of law'; the IRDAI citizen's charter (Policyholders' Interests master circular 2024) also lists 'Insurance Ombudsman / Consumer Court' as options. Order matters the other way: no Ombudsman complaint if the same matter is already before a court or consumer forum (Rule 14(5)).

claim: Once a condition is declared in writing on the proposal form, the insurer can never call it non-disclosure (E058: 'Disclose everything in writing on the proposal form ... Once it's on paper, they can never call it non-disclosure.')
source_quote: Please disclose all pre-existing disease/s or condition/s before buying a policy. Non-disclosure may affect the claim settlement.
note: v2 re-check 2026-10-14: IRDAI CIS format, Annexure-1 to the 29.05.2024 master circular (annexure PDF on this page), item 13 'Your Obligations'. A declared condition is disclosed by definition; the standard wording voids a policy only for 'non-disclosure of any material fact' (Go Digit Arogya Sanjeevani, Disclosure of Information). Cut in v2: v1's 'the company may charge extra, or add a waiting period' (Insurance Products Regulations 2024 Schedule cl. 7: 'Waiting period for pre-existing diseases disclosed by the persons to be insured, shall be maximum up to 36 months of continuous coverage'). Recommended to restore it, so the viewer knows what disclosing costs.

On payment of additional premium, proportionate deduction clause shall stand deleted' (its 1% room cap stays). Cut in v2: v1's 'a cheaper policy with a room rent limit of one percent of the cover' (sourced to the same New India CIS and SBI General).

claim: The only exception is proven fraud that the company has to establish: not a forgotten fever or an undiagnosed ache, but active, deliberate fraud (E035)
source_quote: For the purpose of this clause, the expression "fraud" means any of the following acts committed by the Insured Person or by his agent or the hospital/doctor/any other party acting on behalf of the insured person, with intent to deceive the insurer or to induce the insurer to issue an insurance Policy ... The company shall not repudiate the claim and/or forfeit the policy benefits on the ground of fraud, if the insured person / beneficiary can prove that the misstatement was true to the best of his knowledge and there was no deliberate intention to suppress the fact
note: v2 re-check 2026-10-14: 'Deliberate' matches the wording's 'with intent to deceive' and its honest-misstatement defence. 'Established fraud' is from master circular para 13; the fraud definition (intent to deceive) and the honest-misstatement defence are from the current standard wording (Go Digit 2026; same text in the repealed 2020 IRDAI general-terms guidelines). 'Fraud that the company has to establish' is a fair plain-words reading.

claim: Under official regulations a legal rule makes this exact denial (a non-disclosure ground) illegal once the policy has crossed five years (E009 VO)
source_quote: After completion of sixty continuous months of coverage (including portability and migration) in health insurance policy, no policy and claim shall be contestable by the insurer on grounds of non-disclosure, misrepresentation, except on grounds of established fraud.
note: v2 re-check 2026-10-14: IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations 2024, Schedule cl. 8 (in force 1 Apr 2024). Regulations made under the IRDA Act bind insurers, so a non-disclosure denial after sixty months breaks the law; 'illegal' is fair. The exception (established fraud) follows at E035. Recommended: 'this exact rejection' -> 'this exact denial' (E027 says a cashless denial is not a claim rejection). Its on-screen tag must be this regulation, not the policy wording (HC-01b); set on_screen yes when that tag goes in.

claim: After five years an old health history cannot be used as an excuse; normal policy limits and exclusions still apply; the only exception is proven fraud (E034-E036; card LIMITS, EXCLUSIONS STILL APPLY)
source_quote: Moratorium Period: After completion of Five continuous years under the policy no look back to be applied. ... After the expiry of Moratorium Period no health insurance policy shall be contestable except for proven fraud and permanent exclusions specified in the policy contract.
note: Script fixed 2026-10-14 per the v2 re-check; v2 re-check 2026-10-14: IRDAI CIS format, Annexure-1 to the 29.05.2024 master circular (annexure PDF on this page); its product filing form also asks insurers to 'specify the permanent exclusions'. So exclusions written into the policy survive the moratorium, and E034-E036 as worded tell a viewer whose policy permanently excludes a declared condition that this cannot be used after five years. v1.1 covered it with 'Your normal policy limits and exclusions still apply'; v2 dropped 'and exclusions'. Fix (fact-check.md, v2 required 2): E036 'Your normal policy limits still apply' -> 'Your normal policy limits and exclusions still apply', card LIMITS STILL APPLY -> LIMITS, EXCLUSIONS STILL APPLY. Then set status confirmed. E034-E035 can stay: para 13's only exception to the non-disclosure bar is established fraud.

claim: Of the cases the Ombudsman settled or decided, over seventy-five percent went in favour of the policyholder (E055 VO; board 15,543 of 20,440 settled or decided)
source_quote: Where a complaint is settled through mediation, the Ombudsman shall make a recommendation which it thinks fair in the circumstances of the case ... Where the complaint is not settled by way of mediation under rule 16, the Ombudsman shall pass an award, based on the pleadings and evidence brought on record.
note: Script fixed 2026-10-14 per the v2 re-check; v2 re-check 2026-10-14: Insurance Ombudsman Rules 16(1) and 17(1). The 76% is (9,417 recommendations + 6,126 awards for the complainant) / (9,417 + 6,126 + 4,897 awards for the insurer) = 15,543/20,440 (HC-26). The Rules call recommendations settlements, and the CIO reports them as complaints 'redressed by way of recommendation (mediation)' (Annual Report 2023-24), not as decisions. Of the cases decided by award, 6,126 of 11,023 = 55.6% went for the policyholder, so 'decided cases' reads as about 56%, not over 75%. v1.1 said 'Out of the cases they settled or decided'. Fix (fact-check.md, v2 required 3): 'Of the cases they settled or decided, over seventy-five percent went in favor of the policyholder.'; board label '15,543 of 20,440 settled or decided'. Then set status confirmed.
